nodes.text: #573 : [Er71,p.103] [Er75] [ErSi82] [Er93,p.336] graph theory | turan number A problem of Erdős and Simonovits, who proved that\[\mathrm{ex}(n;\{C_4,C_5\})=(n/2)^{3/2}+O(n).\]Kövári, Sós, and Turán [KST54] proved that the extremal number of edges for containing either $C_4$ or an odd cycle of any length is $\sim (n/2)^{3/2}$. This problem is therefore asking whether the threshold is the same if we just forbid odd cycles of length $3$. See also [574] for the general case, and [765] for $\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)$. This problem is #48 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
